questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To consider not just where I want to visit, but where I want to live and study. Consider how you want to spend your time and if the destination allows that. Consider your finances before going - some places are more expensive than others.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say the Italian attitude to administration is a bit different than in Denmark, and therefore it took some "administrative days" to figure out everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I talked a lot to my fellow exchange goers, and also received some information about courses from the international coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Honestly, it was difficult to figure out which courses i could attend.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Look for something early. Bologna is a really busy student centre, which means the pressure on housing is quite big.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Consider what your budget is, if you want to live with other people, potentially with people from other countries, and how close you want to be to the campus (and if this results in transportation time and costs for you).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were no campus housing available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Make sure you are accepted at UCPH first, but also get a confirmation from Bologna University. Then read the available information about checking in and picking courses. Check which courses you are allowed to have. Fill out the learning agreement and the study plan.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got questions answered by the International Coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There wasn't room for me at one of the courses I wanted, and had to apply for a new approval from the home and host university. Other than that, I could attend the courses of my choice. In Bologna we could change the courses freely before registrering for the exam. But make sure the courses you end up with are approved.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check courses early, and make sure there is room for you to take the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level depends a lot on which courses you take. It is possible to take  courses with a level similar to in Copenhagen, but also to take very easy courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More rote learning in general, less critical thinking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Lifestyles and Health Outcomes, Health Systems, Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging, International Economics, International Finance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Economics and International Finance were interesting mostly because they were held with an Italian Master programme, meaning it was not only exchange students following the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing unexpected. But it was a bit more expensive than i imagined. Going out for dinner (in a cheap place) was almost cheaper than cooking yourself.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was more expensive than imagined. It makes sense, therefore, to exploit that restaurants and bars are cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't use it, if there was any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Honestly, i don't know. But remember that it was somewhat cumbersome to attend sports, since you needed a doctors approval. But didn't look into it more than that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attending a language course could be a nice idea for some. Personally, it took up too much time for it to be a priority of mine, but i know people who benefitted from it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other Italian cities by train. Really easy, and a nice way to explore Italian culture other than the student vibe in Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Pasta, wine, spritz and going out alot was a nice way for us to settle in and feeling welcome.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to go out for dinner, coffee etc. alone. It is way easier to meet people alone or in small groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes Italians are a bit "much". They speak loudly, don't let you through and are always certain that they are right. So you get to practice your confidence.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open in general, which makes it easy to make friends. Also the tradition of aperitivo and 'La Dolce Vita' vibes in general were just as I imagined it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Check courses early and find accommodation before going. Prioritize aperitivo and money spend at restaurants. Be there for as long as you can! I went earlier, which meant I knew the city and some people before uni started, which was perfect to make you feel at home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Administrative stuff will be slow. Be patient. Write e-mails to people when needed. Use other exchange students for ranting.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people! The food! The vibe of going slow and not knowing exactly how you spend your money and time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding out everything by yourself! But realizing that everything works out is very rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
